title: Slow-cooker harissa chickpeas
subtitle: North African spiced chickpeas braised in tomato and harissa
excerpt: Chickpeas cooked slowly in a harissa and tomato base with ras el hanout and lemon. A North African-inspired one-pot that works equally well as a main dish or a side.
sourceNotes: Chickpea dishes spiced with harissa are common across North Africa, particularly in Tunisian and Moroccan cooking where harissa is a staple condiment. The slow-cooker method replicates the long-braised chickpea tagines typical of the region.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight in the fridge and reheat on the hob.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Better the next day as the chickpeas absorb more of the spiced sauce. Reheat with a splash of water if the sauce has thickened too much.

content.text: Tinned chickpeas hold their shape well in a slow cooker. They absorb the harissa and tomato sauce slowly without going mushy. The result is closer to a long-braised tagine than a quick pan dish.

Harissa varies a great deal in heat level. Rose harissa is mild and slightly floral; the tube variety is usually much hotter. Start with 2 tablespoons and taste before adding more. The heat level will mellow somewhat during the long cook.
Serve with flatbreads, couscous, or rice. A spoonful of yoghurt at the table softens the heat.

Add {{onion}} diced onion, {{garlic}} of crushed garlic, {{tinned-tomatoes}} of tinned tomatoes, {{tomato-puree}} of tomato puree, {{harissa}} of harissa, and {{ras-el-hanout}} of ras el hanout to the slow cooker. Pour in {{stock-vegetable}} of vegetable stock and season with {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt. Stir well. Add {{chickpeas-tinned}} of drained chickpeas and stir again.

Set the slow cooker to LOW and cook for 3 to 4 hours. Before serving, squeeze in {{lemon}} of lemon juice and stir through. Taste for seasoning and harissa heat. Scatter {{coriander-fresh}} of fresh coriander over if using.

rows.cause: The harissa used was particularly strong, or too much was added.
rows.fix: Stir in a tablespoon of natural yoghurt or coconut cream to soften the heat. A handful of spinach stirred in also dilutes intensity.

rows.cause: The chickpeas and tomatoes released extra liquid.
rows.fix: Remove the lid and cook on HIGH for 20 to 30 minutes until reduced to your preferred consistency.

rows.cause: They were cooked beyond 4 hours on LOW.
rows.fix: The dish is still good eaten this way; the chickpeas will have absorbed a lot of the sauce. Serve over couscous so the extra sauce is used. Next time check at 3 hours.

rows.cause: The lemon juice was not added at the end, or the salt level is too low.
rows.fix: Squeeze in the juice of a lemon and add a pinch more salt. Stir well and taste again.

content.text: Harissa is the defining condiment of Tunisian cooking and is widely used across North Africa and the Middle East. It is made from dried red chillies, garlic, olive oil, and spices and varies in character from mild and fruity to very fiery. Long-braised chickpeas are common across the region, cooked in tagines and clay pots. The slow cooker replicates this method very well. The dish is satisfying enough to serve as a main course and robust enough to stand alongside grilled or roasted meat.
